outcome: No advance found: the primality/compositeness of the 6th Catalan-Mersenne number (and the general conjecture that all terms past some point are composite) remains undetermined; the number is too large for any known primality test or for GIMPS-style factor searches to have settled.
summary: Catalan's Mersenne conjecture concerns the sequence c0=2, c(n+1)=2^c(n)-1 (2, 3, 7, 127, 2^127-1, ...); the first five terms are known prime, and the conjecture (as Wikipedia frames it) is that some term becomes composite and all terms past that point are composite. Nothing in the window (26 Jan 2024 to 22 Sep 2026) advances this. The current Wikipedia articles for 'Catalan–Mersenne number' (fetched via the live page, last substantively updated per its own text and cross-checked against 'Double Mersenne number', updated 2 Jan 2026) both state plainly that no known method can establish the primality or compositeness of the 6th term (c5 = M(M127)) 'in any reasonable time' because of its size (~10^(10^37.7)), and that no factor below the searched bound has been found for the related double Mersenne candidate MM61. The only item the triage pass surfaced, a May 2024 preprints.org manuscript ('Hyperbolic Primality Test and Catalan–Mersenne Number Conjecture'), proposes a new primality-test heuristic and discusses the conjecture but does not establish compositeness of any further term; it is also unreviewed and, being posted May 2024, is inside the window but does not constitute a resolution, claim of resolution, or bound-moving result on this specific conjecture — I could not fetch the manuscript directly (403 Forbidden) but its title and abstract-level description (via search) confirm it is a proposed method paper, not a settled result, so nothing about it changes the status. A separate item found during this run, a Zenodo preprint by Chua Cheong Siong ('Catalan Mersenne numbers and discovery of the 53rd and 54th Known Mersenne primes', submitted to Inventiones Mathematicae 24 Sep 2025, still under review) claims to have found new (ordinary) Mersenne primes and even 'infinitely many Mersenne primes' — a vastly larger claim than resolving the Mersenne-prime-infinitude problem itself. This has zero uptake in any secondary source, no digestion, is not indexed on arXiv, and a claim of that magnitude going unremarked anywhere in the mathematical community strongly indicates it is not a credible mathematical result; in any case its abstract-level description does not claim to resolve the Catalan-Mersenne conjecture specifically (compositeness of the 6th term), so even taken at face value it would not count under this record's scope. No GIMPS or double-Mersenne search project (mersenne.org, doublemersennes.org) reports a new factor for MM61/MM89/MM107/MM127 in the window. No AI system was found associated with any activity on this problem. The status is 'open' with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: If the Zenodo/Chua preprint's claim of 'infinitely many Mersenne primes' were ever validated by experts, it would settle much more than this conjecture (it would resolve the classical Mersenne-prime infinitude question), and depending on its content it might also bear on double Mersenne numbers/Catalan-Mersenne numbers. But there is no evidence of expert engagement, no arXiv posting, and 'under review' at a journal is not evidence of correctness — extraordinary claims of this kind that lack any community discussion are conventionally treated as unverified/likely incorrect until shown otherwise. I could not open the PDF to check whether it even addresses c5's compositeness (the description only says it discusses Catalan-Mersenne numbers in the title, not that it resolves their conjecture), so this is treated as not counting, per §3.1 and the general evidentiary bar for 'claimed'.
what_would_settle_it: A digested proof or a machine-verified factorization/primality certificate for the 6th Catalan-Mersenne number (or any further term), accepted by number theorists (e.g., discussed on t5k.org/Mersenne Research pages, GIMPS/doublemersennes.org project results, or a peer-reviewed paper); alternatively, expert commentary (positive or negative) on the Chua/Zenodo preprint's claims would clarify whether that work has any bearing at all.
